articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and 'BlueHammer' in Windows Defender — because apparently Patch Tuesday is now Patch Christmas. Chrome also patched its fourth zero-day this year because browsers are basically Swiss cheese at this point.

articles.title: The Internet Still Works: SmugMug Powers Online Photography
articles.summary: Congress is trying to slap a fresh coat of paint on the surveillance state with the 'Foreign Intelligence Accountability Act' — spoiler alert: it's still just warrantless spying with better branding. EFF says reject this fig leaf while we still have Fourth Amendment rights left to protect.

articles.title: EFF Challenges Secrecy In Eastern District of Texas Patent Case
articles.summary: California wants to ban social media for under-16s and force everyone to verify their identity online — because nothing says 'protecting kids' like building a surveillance infrastructure that would make Orwell weep. Privacy dies so legislators can feel good about 'doing something.'

articles.title: 20-Year-Old Malware Rewrites History of Cyber Sabotage
articles.summary: Windows RPC mechanism has an architectural flaw called 'PhantomRPC' with five different privilege escalation paths — because Microsoft's idea of secure design is apparently 'let's see how many ways this can break.' Twenty years of the same mistakes, different CVE numbers.

articles.title: CIA Ran MK-ULTRA Experiments on Prisoners of War in U.S. Custody, Declassified Docs Confirm
articles.summary: Four Democrats hold the keys to Trump's domestic spying dreams as Section 702 hangs in the balance. These are the people who'll decide whether the surveillance state gets a warrantless Christmas or if Americans keep some semblance of privacy rights.

articles.title: SUSE's sovereignty pitch meets an inconvenient $6 billion question
articles.summary: Declassified docs finally confirm the CIA ran MK-ULTRA experiments on North Korean POWs in U.S. custody — because apparently torture needed a research and development department. Only took decades of FOIA fights to drag this particular horror into the light.

articles.title: Medical and utility tech companies admit digital breakins
articles.summary: Checkmarx becomes the latest victim in an ongoing supply-chain attack explicitly targeting security and dev tools — because hackers understand that poisoning the well is more efficient than attacking each village individually. The irony of a security company getting pwned never gets old.

articles.title: After Mythos: New Playbooks For a Zero-Window Era
articles.summary: Hugging Face's LeRobot platform has a critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-25874) with a CVSS of 9.3 — because apparently even our robot overlords ship with default credentials and bad input validation. Nearly 24,000 GitHub stars can't patch stupid.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches Entra ID Role Flaw That Enabled Service Principal Takeover
articles.summary: Chinese Silk Typhoon hacker Xu Zewei gets extradited from Italy for cyberattacks against COVID research — because even during a global pandemic, nation-state actors gonna nation-state. Nothing says 'crimes against humanity' quite like attacking medical research during a health crisis.

articles.title: Morning Minute: NFTs Storm Back, Led by Bored Apes
articles.summary: Claude Mythos AI discovers thousands of zero-days in browsers and operating systems, sending India's CERT-In and major telecos into damage control mode. When your AI assistant becomes better at finding vulnerabilities than your entire security team, it's time to reassess everything.
